# Best CRM for Learning Centers: 6 Systems in Uzbekistan

No single CRM is the best for every learning center. The right choice depends on how many students you have, how many branches you run, how you talk to parents and what you are willing to pay each month. So this article does not rank the systems first and second. It puts six systems offered to learning centers in Uzbekistan side by side and compares them on the same criteria: price, free trial, mobile app and what each one stands out for.

To be upfront: this article was written by the OneRoom team, and OneRoom is one of the systems on the list. Everything about the other systems comes from their own websites and was accurate on October 10, 2026. We have not tested them from the inside, so we do not judge which one is easier to work with. Prices and terms can change, so confirm them with each vendor before you decide.

## Short answer: which system fits whom?

| What matters to you? | Systems to look at | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Knowing the price upfront | OneRoom, EducationCRM | Both publish their plans on the website |
| A longer free trial | EducationCRM, WeWork | 30 and 14 days free |
| Up to 200 students, one branch | OneRoom | The Starter plan is sized for this: 270,000 UZS per month |
| A mobile app for parents or students | WeWork, EducationCRM, LC UP | Their websites mention a dedicated app |
| Rewarding students with coins and prizes | EduCoin, EducationCRM, OneRoom | All three have a rewards section |
| Online lessons | CRM Doctor | Its website lists online lessons through Jitsi Meet |

The table is a starting point, not a recommendation. Each system is covered separately below.

## How did we compare the systems?

We looked for answers to four questions. First: is the price published, and what does the smallest plan cost? Second: how many days can you use it for free? Third: does one system cover a learning center's core work, meaning leads, groups, attendance, payments and debts, and teacher pay? Fourth: how do messages reach parents, and is there a mobile app?

Where a website says nothing, we wrote "not stated" instead of "no". That does not mean the feature is missing. It means you need to ask the vendor.

## Comparison table: price, free trial and features

| System | Smallest plan | Free trial | Mobile app | What its website highlights |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OneRoom | 270,000 UZS/month, up to 200 students | 7 days, no card required | None, runs in the browser | Leads, payments and debts, teacher pay, SMS |
| EducationCRM | 200,000 UZS/month, up to 100 students | 30 days, no card required | Android, for students and teachers | Tests and exams, coins, Telegram bot |
| WeWork | Not stated | 14 days, no card required | Android and iOS, for parents and students | AI assistant, attendance by QR or face, inventory |
| EduCoin | Not stated | 7 days | App for teachers | Coins, rankings and a prize shop |
| CRM Doctor | Not stated | Yes, length not stated | Not stated | Five roles, online lessons, interface in three languages |
| LC UP | Not stated | Free demo | Student and parent apps mentioned | Journal, rooms and finance |

When you compare the two systems with public prices, look at the student limit. EducationCRM's smallest plan is cheaper but covers 100 students. OneRoom's smallest plan costs more but covers 200. With 150 students, the math comes out differently.

## OneRoom

[OneRoom](https://www.oneroom.uz/en) is a CRM and management system for learning centers in Uzbekistan, starting at 270,000 UZS per month with a 7-day free trial. It brings a center's daily work into one place: leads, the student database, courses and groups, a timetable by room, attendance, payments and debts, discounts, expenses, teacher and staff pay, reports and SMS messages. You can upload your student list from an Excel file. The system runs in the browser and opens the same way on a phone and a computer.

There are three plans. Starter is 270,000 UZS per month: up to 200 students, one branch, three admins. Business is 570,000 UZS per month: up to 500 students, three branches, five admins. Premium is 870,000 UZS per month: up to 1,000 students, eight branches, twelve admins. For more than a thousand students the price is agreed separately.

Here are the downsides too. There is no permanent free plan. The free trial is 7 days, one of the shortest on this list. SMS is not included in the plan price and is bought in separate packages: 100 SMS cost 40,000 UZS. There is no dedicated mobile app either. If you want parents to follow along in an app on their phone, look at the systems that have one. The full feature list is on the [CRM for learning centers](https://www.oneroom.uz/en/oquv-markaz-crm) page.

Getting started works like this: you [submit a request](https://www.oneroom.uz/en#contact), a specialist contacts you and sets the system up for your center, and the 7-day free trial begins. No card details are asked for.

## EducationCRM

[EducationCRM](https://educationcrm.uz/) shows its pricing in more detail than any other system here. Its website lists five plans, from 200,000 UZS for up to 100 students to 1,200,000 UZS for up to 2,000 students. According to the website, every plan has the same features and only the size differs. The free trial is 30 days.

It lists separate panels for the director, manager and teacher, tests and exams, a coin system, a Telegram bot and two-factor authentication. SMS is not included in the plan price here either: according to the website, the center connects its own SMS account. The mobile app is listed for Android, and we found nothing about iOS.

## WeWork

The [WeWork](https://we-work.uz/) website says more than 200 learning centers use it. Features we did not see elsewhere: an AI assistant that uses attendance and payments to flag students likely to leave, attendance by QR code or face recognition, and inventory tracking for books and other goods. Integration with Click and Payme is listed as well.

Three plans are named, but the website shows no prices. The parent and student app is available for Android and iOS, and according to the website it is free on the Standard and Professional plans. The free trial is 14 days.

## EduCoin

As the name suggests, [EduCoin](https://educoin.uz/oquv-markaz-crm/) puts the emphasis on motivation: students collect coins, climb a ranking and pick prizes in a shop. Beyond that it covers leads, groups, attendance, payments and debts, expenses, branches and staff roles. The main dashboard shows "at-risk" and "lost" students separately.

Its website says more than 100 educational institutions use it. No price is shown, and you are asked to submit a request. The free trial is 7 days. There is a separate app for teachers.

## CRM Doctor

The [CRM Doctor](https://crm-adds.crm-doctor.uz/) website lists five roles: director, teacher, student, accountant and super admin. What sets it apart is online lessons: a Jitsi Meet link is created inside the system and online attendance is recorded. The interface is available in Uzbek, Russian and English.

The price and the trial length are not stated on the website. It says only that a free trial exists and no card is required. No customer count is given either.

## LC UP

The [LC UP](https://landing.lc-up.com/) website shows four main sections: a dashboard, groups, finance, and a journal with rooms. Student and parent apps are mentioned, but not the devices they run on. When we looked, the pricing section did not load. A free demo is offered.

With so little public information, this system is hard to assess. If you are interested, ask for a demo and put the four questions above to the vendor directly.

## Would Bitrix24, amoCRM, Zoho or HubSpot work?

These are strong systems, but they were built for sales teams. Their core concepts are the lead, the deal and the pipeline stage. A learning center's core concepts are different: the group, the timetable, attendance, the monthly fee and teacher pay. In a general-purpose CRM these are usually added through extra configuration or a separate app. For example, the Bitrix24 marketplace has a [ready-made app for learning centers](https://www.bitrix24.ru/apps/app/152747.gotovaya_crm_dlya_uchebnogo_tsentra/).

A general-purpose CRM can suit you if your center has a separate sales team, you have a person or an integrator to configure it, and you accept running the teaching side in another program. Otherwise, a system made for learning centers that works with groups and attendance from day one takes less effort.

## What should you check yourself before choosing?

Pick two or three systems and run one real group in each free trial. For a week, mark that group's attendance, take one payment, move one student to another group and produce the list of debtors at the end. Did your administrator manage without help? Did the numbers match your own records?

A list of questions for the demo is in our article [12 questions for choosing a CRM](https://www.oneroom.uz/en/blog/oquv-markazi-crm-tanlash). If you still work in Excel and are not sure you need a system, read [Excel or CRM](https://www.oneroom.uz/en/blog/excel-yoki-crm) first.

## Frequently asked questions

How much does a CRM for a learning center cost? In the two systems with public prices, the smallest plan is 200,000 and 270,000 UZS per month, and the largest is 870,000 and 1,200,000 UZS. The other four give a price on request or in a demo.

Is there a free CRM? None of the pages we looked at lists a permanent free plan. Free trials run from 7 to 30 days.

Does a small center need a CRM? That depends on how the work runs, not on the number of students. If you retype the same data in two or three places, or spend half a day building the debtor list, it is worth a try.

Is it hard to switch systems? Many systems can import a student list through Excel, but ask each vendor separately how payment history and balances are carried over.

## Conclusion

If knowing the price upfront matters, start with OneRoom and EducationCRM. If a mobile app comes first, look at WeWork and EducationCRM. If you need a rewards system, add EduCoin to your list. Whichever you choose, let a one-week trial with your own group decide, not the advertising.
